architecture: One existing MQTT Client and original setup/request clocks across immutable request/CONNECT/auth snapshots, numeric/counted DNS/prepared candidates, native verified TLS, strict HTTP Upgrade and MQTT CONNACK/local proof. No MQTT bytes before valid101/Accept/exact mqtt; no compression, redirects, automatic authentication retry, proxy, transport downgrade or extra runtime.
http: Public Core request writer/random key/response parser/Upgrade validator. Contiguous complete response borrows native bytes; fragmented heads use a lazily charged16KiB cache with an incremental delimiter/line-limit probe and one authoritative full semantic parse. Consume exactly through the head, preserving native WS read-ahead. Up to configured bounded informational responses, no clock reset. Header preview can copy some suffix before detecting delimiter; counters report actual preview copies. HTTP state240 persists for snapshots; request/descriptors/cache and key are wiped/freed after handoff or setup stop.
ownership: Existing shared Dial/TLS owned policies and Client post/timer. Native WS attachment consumes the final raw/TLS caller reference, drops the independent pre-Upgrade raw retirement handle only after successful WSS handoff, and retains the original TLS configuration owner until actual WS/TLS retirement. Before handoff, Wait/Poll preserve real raw/TLS alias barriers. Constructor failure consumes no HTTP plan or caller output. Original Client QoS/fences/Auth/Session/Inbox and conservative uncertainty remain unchanged.
publication_fix: TSan found a caller read of WS.Stream racing owner HTTP attachment after Client publication. Final constructor checks only its immutable WS.Native plan, activating inline only for owning-worker raw attachment. Deferred HTTP activation stays exclusively on the owner. Independent select/epoll TSan positive/fault/state tests pass after the correction.

additional_checks.linux_runtime: WSL x64 ASan+UBSan with leak detection, independent TSan; not native Linux production acceptance

real pre-Upgrade raw/TLS aliases block retirement, including single-header tests
initial enhanced AUTH/final-proof/reauth and explicit Session/Inbox replay across HTTP-established connections
legacy TCP/Auth/Session/TLS and raw WS/WSS regression with new selections
plain/full/root singles, stats-off, separate static/shared libraries with real socket protocol consumers, standalone declaration consumers and hidden internal symbols
